messages:
elaine_sec: Heads up — seeing same SSO session_id used from two different countries within ~90s. About 8 distinct user accounts show the same session_id. Possible session replay or stolen cookie.

elaine_sec: Sample auth log snippet:
```auth.log
2026-03-20T18:12:03Z user=alice session_id=b6f9c3a2 ip=35.195.112.45 geo=US req_id=0a1b2c
2026-03-20T18:13:31Z user=bob   session_id=b6f9c3a2 ip=84.30.12.9  geo=NL req_id=0a1b2d
2026-03-20T18:14:10Z user=carol session_id=b6f9c3a2 ip=35.195.112.45 geo=US req_id=0a1b2e
```

jonathan_oncall: On it, creating an incident and paging appropriate folks. @pagerbot please create INC-2026-314 and add Sev2 until we triage.

pagerbot: Incident INC-2026-314 created (severity=Sev2) by @jonathan_oncall. Runbook: https://redwood.internal/incidents/INC-2026-314

mike_infra: Can you paste the full session_id(s) and a couple of req_ids? I'll query CDN and firewall logs for reuse patterns.

elaine_sec: session_id=b6f9c3a2, req_ids=[0a1b2c,0a1b2d,0a1b2e]. Seeing reuse across at least 3 different IPs. No obvious user-agent changes for some hits.

sarah_research: Any recent auth provider or signing key rotations? Could be a bug in session issuance.

mike_infra: No rotations this week. KMS rotation for storage keys last week only. SSO signing key last rotated ~2 months ago (manual). No deployment touching auth pipeline in last 48h.

dmitri_sre: Immediate containment suggestions: 1) Revoke affected sessions and force reauth for those accounts. 2) Block the suspicious IPs at the edge (temporary). 3) Add quick detection for reused session_id across distinct geos. 4) Consider rolling SSO signing key if we see token compromise.

dmitri_sre: Revocation cmd (admin API):
```bash
curl -X POST "https://admin.redwood.internal/v1/sessions/revoke" -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_API" -d '{"session_ids":["b6f9c3a2"], "reason":"suspected replay"}'
```

lina_engineering: If this is a replay we should rotate the SSO JWT signing key via KMS and publish a new jwks url. Steps: generate new KMS key version -> sign new jwks -> grace period for tokens (10m) -> force revoke old tokens. Need platform approval for key push.

mike_infra: I'll block the IPs showing the highest request counts and add an nginx rule to rate-limit session reuse patterns.

elaine_sec: I'm enabling step-up MFA for org-admins and owners now and will start revoking the known session_id across affected users. I'll also open an audit query for token issue events (issuing service, client_id, req_id).

jonathan_oncall: Assign actions: @elaine_sec do revokes+audit query, @mike_infra block IPs + rate-limit, @lina_engineering coordinate KMS key plan, @dmitri_sre update detection rules. I'll handle incident comms and severity.

elaine_sec: Notifying legal/security leadership. No external customer comms yet — we don't have evidence of data exfil.

pagerbot: Incident INC-2026-314 updated: status=investigating, assignees=[elaine_sec,mike_infra,lina_engineering,dmitri_sre], priority=Sev2.

mike_infra: Quick note — edge logs show a small spike from ASN 32934 and ASN 16509 around the same time. I'm pulling PCAPs from the edge boxes for those windows.

sarah_research: After containment, let's run a narrow post-incident eval: prompt sets that touch identity flows + RBAC checks to ensure we didn't silently expand privileges.

elaine_sec: Will follow up with remediation timeline and an initial timeline in the incident doc. Tagging this thread as the primary coordination channel. :lock: :eyes:
